description: Manual expert-review set for §25.1 confidence calibration (F-0552/F-0560). Each case is a hand-labeled situation: the §25.1 component inputs a real pipeline stage would produce, plus the band an expert assigns by POLICY reasoning (high = trustworthy with evidence; moderate = show reservations; low = needs human confirmation; hint = never a basis for decisions). Labels were assigned from the §25.1 policy descriptions, not from the formula.

cases.description: Parcel geometry from ULDK (official register), current, cadastral precision, unambiguous payload.
MPZP indicator extracted deterministically (regex) from the official uchwala text with a verbatim citation.
LLM candidate extraction from a scanned user PDF, weak parser score, ambiguous wording, no verification.
Flood layer from a current informative WFS (not binding), topographic-grade geometry.
Heritage zone digitized from a stale raster source; usable with explicit reservations.
WT rule decided pass/fail from geometry-measured inputs (no assumptions).
WT rule decided, but on the declared conservative windowed_walls assumption instead of measured data.
Hard rule could not be verified (missing input); conservative mode reports a potential blocker.
Expert confirmed the claim, but the underlying sources stay mediocre — confirmation cannot mint authority.
Two independent fresh sources agree on the claim; high-quality geometry.
Sources CONFLICT on the claim (agreement 0.3) — needs human confirmation no matter how good the rest is.
Quick screening with one theme degraded; remaining layers fresh and informative.
Provision from an ARCHIVED, superseded plan — historically interesting, never a basis for decisions.
Geometry from a user-drawn sketch (approximate precision, auxiliary authority).
Survey-grade geometry, official source, expert verified — the best the system can know.
Indicator whose source fragment was security-redacted — citation no longer verifiable.
Nothing measurable (e.g. envelope with zero constraint data) — unknown stays unknown.
Every component mediocre (0.6) — moderate by construction, reservations shown.
Excellent data but the rule itself is essentially unevaluable (certainty 0.05) — the outcome is a hint.
Monitoring detected a change, confirmed by a second source, maximally fresh.
